upstream.commitSubject: fix(schema): apply subscriptions/listen envelope and MetaObject rename to 2026-07-28
upstream.whyACommitAndNotABranch: A digest lock over a moving ref is not a lock. Pinning the immutable commit is what makes every digest below re-derivable by a third party: `git -C <clone> show <commit>:<upstreamPath>` reproduces the exact bytes. Fetching `main` would produce a different tree on every upstream merge and turn each digest into a dated coincidence.
upstream.licenseNote: The vendored LICENSE records a transition from MIT to Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 is what governs these bytes at this commit; the MIT text is retained in the file because upstream retains it, not because it is being asserted here.

files.role: The machine-readable schema. 155 `$defs`. This is the artifact F3 requires be retrievable and summarizable.

The TypeScript source upstream names as AUTHORITATIVE for the revision (schema.json is generated from it). Vendored because it — not schema.json — carries `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28"` at line 30, which is the offline proof of F1 and F2. Without this file the version string would be an assertion in our own artifact rather than a quotation of upstream's.

The changelog F4 requires. Named `.snapshot.md` rather than `.mdx` deliberately: the extension records that this is a frozen copy for offline evidence, and it keeps the bytes out of any tooling that would try to COMPILE an .mdx file.
The deprecation registry. Vendored because F7's evidence is HERE and not, as `finality-status.json` recorded before these bytes existed, in the changelog. See `f7SourceCorrection` below.
Redistribution term for every byte in this directory. Vendored bytes without their license are a compliance defect, not a saving.

invariantCompliance.INV-M4: This lock is what INV-M4 asks for. The prohibition is on CI FETCHING the live spec, not on vendoring: the fetch happened once at authoring time and is recorded here by immutable commit. The gate (tests/invariants/mcp-spec-vendor.invariants.test.ts) reads only these committed bytes and opens no socket.
invariantCompliance.O-M1: "A gate with no evidence artifact is not a gate." Before this directory, F1-F7's PASS rested on a dated manual read. Every digest above is now re-derivable offline by anyone with a checkout.

whatThisLockDoesNotClaim: It does not claim CallLint supports MCP 2026-07-28. `packages/calllint-mcp/src/server.ts` still advertises 2024-11-05, which remains the accurate public state.
It does not claim these bytes were read exhaustively. Five specific offline facts are asserted and gated; the rest of the 181 KB schema is vendored evidence, not audited evidence.

It does not make schema.json a build input. Nothing in `tsconfig.json` (`packages/*/src`, `apps/*/src`, `tests/**`) or `vitest.config.ts` (`packages/**`, `apps/**`, `tests/**`) reaches `third_party/`, so these bytes enter no existing gate — measured, not assumed. Only the named gate above reads them.

f7SourceCorrection.finding: Vendoring falsified the RECORDED REASON for F7 while leaving its verdict standing — the direct payoff O-M1 predicted.
f7SourceCorrection.asRecorded: finality-status.json F7 sourced the deprecation registry to .../2026-07-28/changelog and stated "6 deprecated features and an EMPTY Removed section ... earliest possible removal is the first revision on or after 2027-07-28".
f7SourceCorrection.asMeasured: The changelog has no `Removed` heading at all and 4 numbered deprecation items. The registry is `deprecated.mdx`: `## Deprecated` (exactly 6 feature rows) + `## Removed` ("No features have been removed under this policy yet."). So the count and the empty Removed section are RIGHT and the URL was WRONG.
f7SourceCorrection.overPreciseSubClaim: 4 of the 6 rows read "First revision released on or after 2027-07-28". The other two do not: `includeContext` follows Sampling, and HTTP+SSE reads "Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final" — a date this registry does not record. "Earliest possible removal is 2027-07-28" was therefore stated more precisely than the source supports.
f7SourceCorrection.whyTheVerdictSurvives: F7 asks for no pending breaking ERRATUM. Deprecation is not removal: upstream states removal happens in a future revision by Core Maintainer decision, and the Removed section is empty. Nothing breaks WITHIN 2026-07-28 on either clock, so the unknown SEP-2596 date cannot change the verdict — only the precision of the sentence describing it.
